title: Neutral-pronoun control and accuracy check for twin averaging
description: Add a neutral-pronoun arm (they, and blanked) beside he and she on the bios task to show which direction the pronoun bias runs, and score the twin-averaged verdict against the corpus occupation label to check that removing the variable does not cost accuracy. Prompted by a reader asking whether stripping sex creates more equal distributions. Pre-register before any run; Laya only.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Pronoun control arms
  Scenario: Neutral pronouns show the direction of the bias
    Given the same 2000 bios with the pronoun set to he, she, they and blanked
    When Laya answers paralegal or attorney for each arm
    Then the neutral verdict rate is reported beside he and she with intervals
  Scenario: Twin averaging does not cost accuracy
    Given the twin-averaged verdict for each bio
    When it is scored against the corpus occupation label
    Then accuracy is reported beside the single-pronoun verdicts

comments.author: home
comments.text: Pre-registration committed (03a4971, amended 5d3de09 on feat/neutral-pronoun). Cue built for seven tasks: blank arm drops no bios; they arm drops 0.2-1.3% (fails the 1% rule on journalist and architect). Grammar audit of 350 they rewrites: about 18% show unadjusted verbs after and/comma, over the 10% threshold, so the they arm is exploratory. Laya answers rerunning after fixing the record question name (Occupation). Scoring: metrics/neutral.py with specs; replay wiring in progress.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Merged to main (33d0fdf): neutral cue, Laya answers, position and shortlist scoring, replayed studies, and a neutral table on the gender pages. Predictions: neutral-between refuted for the person arm (3 of 6), the two neutral wordings disagree by 3-4.5 pts per bio (refuted), paralegal cost prediction held (accuracy -3.7, ratio 0.72). Direction differs by occupation: near she for nurse/teacher/dietitian, at he for architect, mid for surgeon/paralegal. Remaining: the direction and cost charts on the Gender page.

right_now_summary: The Gender page still needs charts showing bias direction and the accuracy cost of twin averaging.
